text:
ashley: Heads-up from last night's autotune sweep (int4+fp8) on sm95: p99 latency regressed for long inputs. When selector picks fp8_streamlined with workspace_budget=0.5 for seq=4096 we see p99 +28% vs int4 baseline. Trace ids attached.

ravi: Do you have the selector config and a short profiler extract? Is this allocation or compute-bound?

ashley: Profiler snippet below (trimmed):
```
selector: autotune-shadow-3
heuristics: { workspace_budget: 0.5, seq_buckets: [256,1024,3072], kv_warmup: delayed }
picked: fp8_streamlined_sm95
observed: p50 210ms p95 340ms p99 520ms (seq=4096)  # baseline int4 p99 405ms
```
perf-bot: nightly-autotune: sm95 int4+fp8 sweep complete 02 regressions flagged: p99 +28% (seq=4096)

jordan: Is steady throughput affected or just tail? Also did you try forcing int4/fp8 to isolate?

ashley: Throughput steady. Forced int4 path wins at 4096 (p99 ~405ms). Forced fp8 is better at short seq (<512) but at 4096 fp8_streamlined triggers a workspace reallocation after KV warmup and stalls the tail.

liam: My read: fp8_streamlined uses a compact workspace layout that defers some KV placement; when workspace_budget < 1.0 and seq > bucket it performs a staging copy for KV which is serialized on the compute stream. That aligns with the p99 spikes.

anya: I'll run a focused microbench toggling kv_warmup & workspace_budget across archs. Plan: sm83, sm86, sm92, sm95; seqs [512,2048,4096]; batch=1. Will push CSVs to perf-storage.

ashley: Repro command used locally:
```
./perfbench --model gptx-q --arch sm95 --quant fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --selector autotune-shadow-3 
# then --kv-warmup=on/off --workspace_budget=0.5/0.9
```
Observed: kv_warmup=on & workspace_budget=0.9 => p99 430ms; kv_warmup=off & workspace_budget=0.5 => p99 520ms.

ravi: Ok, conservative mitigation: rollback selector-canary to previous stable (autotune-shadow-2) for canary pool until we add a safety rule. I'll flip at 07:00 UTC and watch traces.

liam: Safety rule idea: if seq > 2048 and workspace_budget < 0.7 on sm95, prefer int4_kernel. Also add a per-arch override table because sm95 staging costs are higher in our tests.

jordan: And add hysteresis counters: require N consecutive picks before switching kernel for long-seq traffic, plus a backoff timeout to avoid flip-flopping when KV warms. That reduced jitter before for batching heuristic.

ashley: Also recommend selector telemetry emit: predicted_workspace_bytes, actual_resident_bytes, staging_copy_count per request. That will help detect mispredictions during autotune.

anya: Will include those metrics in the microbench outputs so we can correlate p99 with staging_copy_count.

perf-bot: action-ack: anya, liam, ravi

ashley: Action items:
- anya: run cross-arch microbench and upload per-arch CSVs + metric outlines (due EOD)
- liam: implement safety rule + hysteresis + telemetry hooks in selector (PR and unit tests)
- ravi: rollback canary to stable selector and monitor (on-call)

jordan: One more ask 2D add a telemetry alert when predicted_workspace / actual_resident > 1.2 for >5% of requests in 5m window. That should catch bad kernel picks early.

ashley: Agreed. I'll file a follow-up issue with preliminary thresholds after we see anya's CSVs.
